```java
        Objects.requireNonNull(
                originalCapital,
                "originalCapital cannot be null");

        Objects.requireNonNull(
                profitOrLoss,
                "profitOrLoss cannot be null");

        if (grossRealization.signum() < 0
                || liabilitiesSettled.signum() < 0
                || originalCapital.signum() < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Amounts cannot be negative");
        }

        BigDecimal expectedNet =
                grossRealization.subtract(liabilitiesSettled);

        if (expectedNet.compareTo(netRealization) != 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Net realization does not reconcile");
        }
    }

    public boolean isProfit() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() > 0;
    }

    public boolean isLoss() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() < 0;
    }

    public boolean isBreakEven() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() == 0;
    }
}
```

But one important point:

**Do not blindly define**

```text
profitOrLoss = netRealization - originalCapital
```

for every Syirkah type.

The source explicitly describes that calculation for the particular Mudharabah dissolution arrangement, while other Syirkah types may have different contract/accounting treatment. Hukum-muamalah

So the actual calculation should be delegated:

```java
public interface SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy {

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidationResult> determine(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion);
}
```

This keeps the **contract-specific Sharia rule** out of the generic liquidation state machine.

---

# 6. Capital return becomes a separate obligation

We should not reuse `PartnerDistributionObligation`.

Create:

```java
public final class PartnerCapitalReturnObligation {

    private final String obligationId;
    private final String liquidationId;
    private final String partyId;
    private final BigDecimal capitalAmount;

    private CapitalReturnStatus status;

    private String approvedBy;
    private String postedJournalEntryId;

    public PartnerCapitalReturnObligation(
            String obligationId,
            String liquidationId,
            String partyId,
            BigDecimal capitalAmount) {

        this.obligationId =
                requireText(obligationId, "obligationId");

        this.liquidationId =
                requireText(liquidationId, "liquidationId");

        this.partyId =
                requireText(partyId, "partyId");

        Objects.requireNonNull(
                capitalAmount,
                "capitalAmount cannot be null");

        if (capitalAmount.signum() <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "capitalAmount must be positive");
        }

        this.capitalAmount = capitalAmount;
        this.status = CapitalReturnStatus.CALCULATED;
    }

    public void approve(String approver) {
        if (status != CapitalReturnStatus.CALCULATED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return must be CALCULATED");
        }

        this.approvedBy =
                requireText(approver, "approver");

        this.status = CapitalReturnStatus.APPROVED;
    }

    public void markPosted(String journalEntryId) {
        if (status != CapitalReturnStatus.APPROVED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return must be APPROVED");
        }

        this.postedJournalEntryId =
                requireText(
                        journalEntryId,
                        "journalEntryId");

        this.status = CapitalReturnStatus.POSTED;
    }

    public void settle() {
        if (status != CapitalReturnStatus.POSTED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return must be POSTED");
        }

        this.status = CapitalReturnStatus.SETTLED;
    }

    // getters...
}
```

```java
public enum CapitalReturnStatus {
    CALCULATED,
    APPROVED,
    POSTED,
    SETTLED,
    CANCELLED
}
```

This preserves the distinction:

```text
profit allocation
        ≠
capital return
        ≠
cash settlement
```

---

# 7. Final termination reconciliation

Before `CAPITAL_RETURN` can complete, require:

```text
net realizable business assets
    =
liabilities settled
+ partner distributions
+ partner capital returns
+ explicitly retained amount
```

The exact formula can be policy-specific, but the invariant should be explicit.

Create:

```java
public record SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
        BigDecimal netRealization,
        BigDecimal totalProfitDistribution,
        BigDecimal totalLossAbsorption,
        BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn,
        BigDecimal remainingBalance,
        boolean balanced,
        List<String> errors
) {

    public SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation {
        errors = List.copyOf(errors);

        if (balanced && !errors.isEmpty()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Balanced reconciliation cannot contain errors");
        }
    }
}
```

No tolerance should silently hide money.

If there is a 0.01 difference, we need either:

- deterministic rounding policy, or
- explicit reconciliation adjustment.

Never:

```java
difference = BigDecimal.ZERO;
```

just to make the close pass.

---

# 9. Application service

The complete API becomes:

```java
public interface SyirkahLiquidationService {

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidation> start(
            StartLiquidationRequest request);

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidation> beginAssetRealization(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<LiquidationRealization> recordRealization(
            RecordLiquidationRealizationRequest request);

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidation> completeAssetRealization(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<LiquidationLiabilitySettlement> settleLiability(
            RecordLiabilitySettlementRequest request);

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidation> completeLiabilitySettlement(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidationResult> determineResult(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<List<PartnerDistributionObligation>> prepareDistribution(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<List<PartnerCapitalReturnObligation>> prepareCapitalReturn(
            String liquidationId);

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidation> complete(
            String liquidationId);
}
```

Again, no single method automatically performs the entire termination.

---

# 10. How it connects to the existing close snapshot

This is the important historical boundary:

```text
                 OLD SYIRKAH
                     │
              Locked Close
                     │
                     ▼
          SyirkahCloseSnapshot
                     │
              immutable history
                     │
                     ▼
               Liquidation
                     │
       ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
       ▼                           ▼
Asset realization          Liability settlement
       │                           │
       └─────────────┬─────────────┘
                     ▼
             Final reconciliation
                     │
                     ▼
              Final result
                     │
              ┌──────┴──────┐
              ▼             ▼
          Profit/Loss    Capital return
              │             │
              └──────┬──────┘
                     ▼
                TERMINATED
```

The snapshot is never rewritten.

---

# 11. New contract starts from a new opening

For a transition rather than termination:

```text
Old contract
     │
     ▼
locked snapshot
     │
     ▼
settlement
     │
     ▼
old contract closed
     │
     ▼
new contract
     │
     ▼
new opening position
```

This matches the source's explicit principle that when new capital or a new partner enters, the old Syirkah is first closed and the new Syirkah gets new bookkeeping. Hukum-muamalah

So we should **not** create:

```text
old contract version 1
        ↓
same running ledger
        ↓
new partner
```

as though nothing happened.

Instead:

```text
contract A / version 1
        ↓
close snapshot A
        ↓
transition
        ↓
contract B / version 1
```

---

# 12. Partner replacement becomes especially clean

For replacement:

```text
Existing partners approve
        ↓
Syufah / transfer restriction policy
        ↓
Old Syirkah close
        ↓
Frozen position
        ↓
Transfer / settlement
        ↓
Old partner exits
        ↓
New partner enters
        ↓
New Syirkah contract
```

The source specifically states that an external sale of a partner's share requires consent of the other partners and discusses their pre-emptive right; after agreement, the Syirkah is closed first so its latest financial position can be determined. Hukum-muamalah

Therefore our existing:

```java
PartnerTransferRestrictionPolicy
```

is not optional decoration—it is the right architectural boundary for this rule.

---

## 13. Final lifecycle

At this point the Syirkah extension has a complete lifecycle:

```text
CONTRACT ACTIVE
      │
      ├── normal period
      │       ↓
      │   close result
      │       ↓
      │   allocation
      │       ↓
      │   partner positions
      │       ↓
      │   immutable snapshot
      │       ↓
      │   CLOSE LOCKED
      │
      ├── continue
      │       ↓
      │   next period
      │
      ├── partner/capital transition
      │       ↓
      │   settlement
      │       ↓
      │   new contract
      │
      └── full termination
              ↓
          liquidation
              ↓
       asset realization
              ↓
       liability settlement
              ↓
        final result
              ↓
        distribution
              ↓
        capital return
              ↓
          TERMINATED
```

### One important source-derived rule

The source's accounting example defines net profit as:

```text
Total Revenue
- Direct Costs
- Operating Costs
- Other Costs
= Net Profit
```

and explicitly distinguishes profit sharing from loss treatment. Hukum-muamalah

So the implementation should continue using our existing:

```text
FinancialResult
SyirkahResultCalculator
LossAllocationPolicyResolver
```

rather than introducing a second liquidation-specific profit formula.

**Next I would implement the transition/termination orchestration and its invariants**, including the exact `SyirkahTransitionServiceImpl`, `SyirkahLiquidationServiceImpl`, and the idempotency/transaction boundaries connecting them to the existing close snapshot and journal posting.

//////////////


Next, I would implement the **Syirkah liquidation settlement/accounting bridge**.

The liquidation aggregate should remain business-state oriented. Accounting should be a separate policy/application layer, just like profit distribution.

### 1. Capital-return accounting policy

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.util.List;

public interface SyirkahCapitalReturnAccountingPolicy {

    JournalMapping map(List<PartnerCapitalReturnObligation> obligations);

    record JournalMapping(
            String description,
            List<JournalLineMapping> lines
    ) {
        public JournalMapping {
            if (description == null || description.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Description cannot be blank");
            }
            if (lines == null || lines.isEmpty()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Journal mapping must contain lines");
            }
            lines = List.copyOf(lines);
        }
    }

    record JournalLineMapping(
            String accountId,
            LineType type,
            String amount,
            String currencyCode,
            String description
    ) {
        public JournalLineMapping {
            if (accountId == null || accountId.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Account ID cannot be blank");
            }
            if (amount == null || amount.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Amount cannot be blank");
            }
            if (currencyCode == null || currencyCode.isBlank()) {
                throw new IllegalArgumentException("Currency code cannot be blank");
            }
        }
    }

    enum LineType {
        DEBIT,
        CREDIT
    }
}
```

This deliberately does **not** decide that every capital return is:

```text
Dr Partner Capital
Cr Cash
```

because the actual accounting treatment can depend on the ledger design, impairment, retained balances, settlement mechanism, and contract policy.

---

### 2. Capital-return posting service

The flow should be:

```text
Liquidation result
      ↓
Capital return obligations
      ↓
Approval
      ↓
Accounting policy
      ↓
Journal posting
      ↓
Obligations marked POSTED
      ↓
Cash settlement
```

Not:

```text
Liquidation → automatically pay partners
```

The proposed application service:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.identifier.JournalEntryId;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.PartnerCapitalReturnObligation;

import java.util.List;

public interface SyirkahCapitalReturnPostingService {

    Uni<JournalEntryId> post(
            String tenantId,
            String ledgerId,
            String liquidationId,
            String postedBy
    );

    Uni<List<PartnerCapitalReturnObligation>> findObligations(
            String tenantId,
            String ledgerId,
            String liquidationId
    );
}
```

The implementation should enforce:

```text
all obligations APPROVED
        ↓
map accounting
        ↓
post one idempotent journal
        ↓
mark every obligation POSTED
```

Use:

```text
sourceType = SYIRKAH_CAPITAL_RETURN
sourceId   = liquidationId
```

and the same database-backed source uniqueness we established for other Syirkah accounting operations.

---

### 3. Do not confuse capital return with profit distribution

This is important for the model.

Suppose:

```text
Original capital       100m
Final net assets       130m
Profit                 30m
```

The liquidation may produce:

```text
Profit allocation      30m
Capital return        100m
```

Those are **two different obligations**.

Therefore:

```text
PartnerDistributionObligation
```

and:

```text
PartnerCapitalReturnObligation
```

must remain separate aggregates.

Likewise:

```text
PROFIT_ALLOCATION
CAPITAL_RETURN
CASH_SETTLEMENT
```

remain separate `PartnerAccountMovement` types.

---

### 4. Add liquidation reconciliation

Before capital return is approved, introduce:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.List;

public record SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
        BigDecimal netRealization,
        BigDecimal totalProfitDistribution,
        BigDecimal totalLossAbsorption,
        BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn,
        BigDecimal remainingBalance,
        boolean balanced,
        List<String> errors
) {

    public SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation {
        netRealization = requireNonNegative(netRealization, "Net realization");
        totalProfitDistribution = requireNonNegative(
                totalProfitDistribution,
                "Total profit distribution"
        );
        totalLossAbsorption = requireNonNegative(
                totalLossAbsorption,
                "Total loss absorption"
        );
        totalCapitalReturn = requireNonNegative(
                totalCapitalReturn,
                "Total capital return"
        );
        remainingBalance = requireNonNegative(
                remainingBalance,
                "Remaining balance"
        );
        errors = errors == null ? List.of() : List.copyOf(errors);
    }

    private static BigDecimal requireNonNegative(
            BigDecimal value,
            String field
    ) {
        if (value == null || value.signum() < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    field + " must not be negative"
            );
        }
        return value;
    }
}
```

The key invariant is:

```text
net realization
=
profit distribution
+ capital return
+ remaining balance
```

for the profit case, with the exact loss-side treatment determined by the liquidation policy.

The reconciliation must explicitly represent any residual instead of silently forcing it to zero.

---

### 5. Complete liquidation lifecycle

At this point the lifecycle becomes:

```text
NORMAL CLOSE
    ↓
Locked Syirkah Close Snapshot
    ↓
Syirkah Liquidation
    ↓
Asset Realization
    ↓
Liability Settlement
    ↓
Final Reconciliation
    ↓
Liquidation Result
    ↓
┌───────────────────────┐
│ Profit                │
│   ↓                   │
│ Profit Distribution   │
│   ↓                   │
│ Capital Return        │
│   ↓                   │
│ Cash Settlement       │
│                       │
│ OR                    │
│                       │
│ Loss                  │
│   ↓                   │
│ Loss Allocation /     │
│ Responsibility        │
│   ↓                   │
│ Capital Return        │
└───────────────────────┘
    ↓
Old Contract Terminated
```

And for a partner replacement:

```text
Old Contract
    ↓
Locked Close Snapshot
    ↓
Settlement
    ↓
Old Contract Closed
    ↓
Transfer / Exit / Entry
    ↓
New Contract
    ↓
New Opening Position
```

### 6. One important correction to the previous design

The framework already has a generic `UnitOfWork` abstraction:

```java
tech.kayys.syirkah.foundation.application.transaction.UnitOfWork
```

So we **should use that existing abstraction**, rather than introducing a separate `AccountingUnitOfWork`.

That keeps the new Syirkah implementation aligned with the existing platform architecture.

The next concrete layer after this should therefore be the **`SyirkahLiquidationService` application orchestration + repository ports**, including idempotent state transitions and the final `COMPLETE` invariant.

Next is the **`SyirkahLiquidationService` application orchestration layer**.

The domain aggregate already defines the state machine. The application layer should now enforce the workflow, persistence, idempotency, and separation between liquidation, accounting, and settlement.

### 3. Start request

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.time.LocalDate;
import java.util.Objects;

public record StartLiquidationRequest(
        String tenantId,
        String ledgerId,
        String liquidationId,
        String contractId,
        int contractVersion,
        String closeCycleId,
        LocalDate liquidationDate,
        String requestedBy
) {

    public StartLiquidationRequest {
        require(tenantId, "Tenant ID");
        require(ledgerId, "Ledger ID");
        require(liquidationId, "Liquidation ID");
        require(contractId, "Contract ID");
        require(closeCycleId, "Close cycle ID");
        require(requestedBy, "Requested by");

        Objects.requireNonNull(liquidationDate, "Liquidation date cannot be null");

        if (contractVersion <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Contract version must be positive"
            );
        }
    }

    private static void require(String value, String name) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(name + " cannot be blank");
        }
    }
}
```

---

### 4. Critical invariant: liquidation requires a locked close

This is where the application service should connect the previous work.

Do **not** allow:

```text
Open close
   ↓
Liquidation
```

Require:

```text
CloseCycle
   ↓
SYIRKAH_RESULT
   ↓
SYIRKAH_ALLOCATION
   ↓
SYIRKAH_DISTRIBUTION
   ↓
VALIDATION
   ↓
APPROVAL
   ↓
LOCKED
   ↓
Liquidation
```

The service therefore needs a port:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.port;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;

public interface SyirkahCloseStateProvider {

    Uni<Boolean> isLocked(
            String tenantId,
            String ledgerId,
            String closeCycleId
    );
}
```

Then:

```java
if (!locked) {
    return Uni.createFrom().failure(
            new IllegalStateException(
                    "Syirkah liquidation requires a locked close cycle"
            )
    );
}
```

This prevents liquidation from bypassing the normal accounting close.

---

### 5. Idempotent `start`

The important pattern is:

```text
find existing
     │
     ├── exists → return existing
     │
     └── absent
           ↓
       validate close
           ↓
       create liquidation
           ↓
       save
```

Conceptually:

```java
return liquidationRepository
        .findById(
                request.tenantId(),
                request.ledgerId(),
                request.liquidationId()
        )
        .chain(existing -> {
            if (existing.isPresent()) {
                return Uni.createFrom().item(existing.get());
            }

            return closeStateProvider.isLocked(
                    request.tenantId(),
                    request.ledgerId(),
                    request.closeCycleId()
            ).chain(locked -> {
                if (!locked) {
                    return Uni.createFrom().failure(
                            new IllegalStateException(
                                    "Liquidation requires a locked close cycle"
                            )
                    );
                }

                SyirkahLiquidation liquidation =
                        SyirkahLiquidation.start(
                                request.liquidationId(),
                                request.tenantId(),
                                request.ledgerId(),
                                request.contractId(),
                                request.contractVersion(),
                                request.closeCycleId(),
                                request.liquidationDate()
                        );

                return liquidationRepository
                        .save(liquidation)
                        .replaceWith(liquidation);
            });
        });
```

The database still needs a uniqueness constraint. The application-level lookup is **not** sufficient against concurrent requests.

```sql
UNIQUE (
    tenant_id,
    ledger_id,
    liquidation_id
);

UNIQUE (
    tenant_id,
    ledger_id,
    contract_id,
    status
);
```

The second constraint should be implemented more carefully as a database partial/conditional unique index if the database supports it, so only active liquidation states conflict.

---

### 6. Realization must be idempotent too

A realization should have its own business source/reference:

```java
public record RecordLiquidationRealizationRequest(
        String tenantId,
        String ledgerId,
        String realizationId,
        String liquidationId,
        String assetReference,
        BigDecimal carryingValue,
        BigDecimal realizedAmount,
        LocalDate realizationDate,
        String sourceReference
) {}
```

Database:

```sql
UNIQUE (
    tenant_id,
    ledger_id,
    realization_id
);
```

And preferably:

```sql
UNIQUE (
    tenant_id,
    ledger_id,
    liquidation_id,
    source_reference
);
```

That protects against a retry accidentally realizing the same asset twice.

---

### 7. Liability settlement has the same rule

```text
Outstanding liability
        ↓
Settlement instruction
        ↓
Actual settled amount
        ↓
Cannot exceed outstanding amount
```

Never allow:

```text
settledAmount > outstandingAmount
```

and never allow a second identical settlement simply because the first request timed out.

---

### 8. Result determination

This should **not** be implemented directly inside the service.

Use:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;

public interface SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy {

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidationResult> determine(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    );
}
```

So:

```text
LiquidationService
       ↓
ResultPolicy
       ↓
SyirkahLiquidationResult
```

This is important because the calculation of final partner entitlement should remain **contract/policy-specific**, particularly for Mudharabah versus Musyarakah/Inan and responsibility cases.

---

### 9. Completion invariant

The final operation should be deliberately strict:

```text
RESULT_DETERMINED
        ↓
DISTRIBUTION completed
        ↓
CAPITAL_RETURN completed
        ↓
COMPLETE
```

Therefore `completeCapitalReturn()` should verify:

```text
1. liquidation result exists
2. reconciliation is balanced
3. all profit/loss obligations are completed
4. all capital-return obligations are POSTED
5. no unresolved liability remains
6. no unresolved asset realization remains
7. operator is supplied
```

Only then:

```java
liquidation.completeCapitalReturn(completedBy);
```

This gives us the final invariant:

```text
COMPLETE
  ⇔
final financial position reconciled
AND
result determined
AND
partner result obligations completed
AND
capital return obligations completed
AND
no unresolved liquidation balance
```

### Where this puts us

The Syirkah financial lifecycle is now becoming coherent:

```text
Contract
   ↓
Periodic Close
   ↓
Financial Result
   ↓
Partner Allocation
   ↓
Close Position
   ↓
Immutable Close Snapshot
   ↓
LOCKED
   │
   ├── Continue Syirkah
   │
   ├── Partner Entry/Exit
   │
   └── Full Liquidation
           ↓
       Realization
           ↓
       Liability Settlement
           ↓
       Final Reconciliation
           ↓
       Final Result
           ↓
       Distribution
           ↓
       Capital Return
           ↓
       Terminated
```

The next piece I would implement is **`SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy` + final liquidation reconciliation**, because that is the point where the system must formally distinguish **net assets, profit/loss, partner allocation, and capital return** before any money can be settled.



//////////////

The source supports the distinction we need: in **Mudharabah**, ordinary business loss is borne by capital providers, while the manager becomes responsible when loss results from intentional misconduct or violation of the agreed conditions. Hukum-muamalah

So the next implementation should be a **policy-based liquidation result**, not a generic `netRealization - capital` formula.

### 1. Result model

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.Objects;

public record SyirkahLiquidationResult(
        String liquidationId,
        String contractId,
        int contractVersion,
        BigDecimal grossRealization,
        BigDecimal liabilitiesSettled,
        BigDecimal netRealization,
        BigDecimal originalCapital,
        BigDecimal profitOrLoss
) {

    public SyirkahLiquidationResult {
        require(liquidationId, "Liquidation ID");
        require(contractId, "Contract ID");

        if (contractVersion <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Contract version must be positive"
            );
        }

        requireNonNegative(grossRealization, "Gross realization");
        requireNonNegative(liabilitiesSettled, "Liabilities settled");
        requireNonNegative(originalCapital, "Original capital");

        Objects.requireNonNull(profitOrLoss, "Profit or loss cannot be null");

        BigDecimal expectedNet =
                grossRealization.subtract(liabilitiesSettled);

        if (expectedNet.compareTo(netRealization) != 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Net realization must equal gross realization minus liabilities settled"
            );
        }

        if (netRealization.signum() < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Net realization cannot be negative"
            );
        }
    }

    public boolean isProfit() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() > 0;
    }

    public boolean isLoss() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() < 0;
    }

    public boolean isBreakEven() {
        return profitOrLoss.signum() == 0;
    }

    private static void require(String value, String name) {
        if (value == null || value.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(name + " cannot be blank");
        }
    }

    private static void requireNonNegative(
            BigDecimal value,
            String name
    ) {
        if (value == null || value.signum() < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    name + " must not be negative"
            );
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. Policy contract

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.close.SyirkahCloseSnapshot;

public interface SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy {

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidationResult> determine(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    );
}
```

This keeps the domain rule explicit:

```text
Liquidation
   +
Opening position
   +
Contract version
        ↓
Liquidation result policy
        ↓
Final profit/loss
```

### 3. Default policy for capital-based Syirkah

For contracts where the liquidation result is determined from the final net realization against the capital position:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.close.SyirkahCloseSnapshot;

import java.math.BigDecimal;

public final class CapitalBasedLiquidationResultPolicy
        implements SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy {

    @Override
    public Uni<SyirkahLiquidationResult> determine(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    ) {
        BigDecimal originalCapital =
                openingSnapshot.positions().stream()
                        .map(position -> position.openingCapital())
                        .reduce(BigDecimal.ZERO, BigDecimal::add);

        BigDecimal netRealization =
                liquidation.getNetRealization();

        BigDecimal profitOrLoss =
                netRealization.subtract(originalCapital);

        return Uni.createFrom().item(
                new SyirkahLiquidationResult(
                        liquidation.getLiquidationId(),
                        liquidation.getContractId(),
                        liquidation.getContractVersion(),
                        liquidation.getGrossRealization(),
                        liquidation.getLiabilitiesSettled(),
                        netRealization,
                        originalCapital,
                        profitOrLoss
                )
        );
    }
}
```

But this policy should **not** be universally assigned to every `SyirkahType`.

### 4. Resolver

We already established the pattern of resolving loss behavior by contract type. Extend that pattern here:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;

public interface SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver {

    SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy resolve(
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    );
}
```

Then:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahType;

import java.util.Map;
import java.util.Objects;

public final class DefaultSyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver
        implements SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver {

    private final Map<SyirkahType, SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy> policies;

    public DefaultSyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver(
            Map<SyirkahType, SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy> policies
    ) {
        this.policies = Map.copyOf(
                Objects.requireNonNull(policies)
        );
    }

    @Override
    public SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy resolve(
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    ) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(contractVersion);

        SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicy policy =
                policies.get(contractVersion.type());

        if (policy == null) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "No liquidation result policy configured for Syirkah type: "
                            + contractVersion.type()
            );
        }

        return policy;
    }
}
```

If the current `SyirkahContract.Version` does not expose `type()`, use the existing contract-level type accessor rather than adding a duplicate field.

### 5. Do not silently use the current PartnerAccount

The calculation should use:

```text
Locked historical snapshot
        ↓
opening capital
```

not:

```text
Current PartnerAccount
```

That preserves the previously established invariant:

```text
PartnerAccount = rebuildable projection
CloseSnapshot = historical financial position
```

### 6. Final reconciliation

Once the result is determined:

```text
Net realization
      ↓
Profit/Loss
      ↓
Partner allocations
      +
Capital returns
      +
Any remaining balance
      ↓
Final reconciliation
```

For a profit example:

```text
Net realization       130m
Original capital      100m
Profit                 30m
```

Then:

```text
Profit allocation       30m
Capital return          100m
Remaining balance        0
```

For a loss:

```text
Net realization        70m
Original capital      100m
Loss                   30m
```

The `30m` is **loss**, not a negative capital-return obligation. The capital return is limited by the remaining capital position.

That distinction is essential.

### 7. Next layer

After this, the next implementation should be the **`SyirkahLiquidationAllocationService`**:

```text
SyirkahLiquidationResult
        ↓
contract-specific allocation
        ↓
PartnerDistributionObligation
        +
PartnerCapitalReturnObligation
        +
LossResponsibility / Recovery
        ↓
Final LiquidationReconciliation
```

That will connect the existing profit/loss allocation engine to liquidation without duplicating its business rules.

//////////////

The next layer is the **liquidation allocation service**. The important design point is that liquidation produces three different financial outcomes:

1. **Profit allocation**
2. **Loss allocation / responsibility**
3. **Capital return**

They must never be collapsed into one “partner payout”.

### 1. Allocation result

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.distribution.PartnerDistributionObligation;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.capital.PartnerCapitalReturnObligation;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.loss.SyirkahLossResponsibility;

import java.util.List;

public record SyirkahLiquidationAllocation(
        String liquidationId,
        SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
        List<PartnerDistributionObligation> profitDistributions,
        List<PartnerCapitalReturnObligation> capitalReturns,
        List<SyirkahLossResponsibility> lossResponsibilities
) {

    public SyirkahLiquidationAllocation {
        if (liquidationId == null || liquidationId.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Liquidation ID cannot be blank"
            );
        }

        if (result == null) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Liquidation result cannot be null"
            );
        }

        profitDistributions =
                List.copyOf(profitDistributions == null
                        ? List.of()
                        : profitDistributions);

        capitalReturns =
                List.copyOf(capitalReturns == null
                        ? List.of()
                        : capitalReturns);

        lossResponsibilities =
                List.copyOf(lossResponsibilities == null
                        ? List.of()
                        : lossResponsibilities);
    }
}
```

This deliberately does **not** use a generic `PartnerSettlement`.

---

## 2. Allocation service

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.SyirkahLiquidation;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.SyirkahLiquidationAllocation;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.SyirkahLiquidationResult;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.close.SyirkahCloseSnapshot;

public interface SyirkahLiquidationAllocationService {

    Uni<SyirkahLiquidationAllocation> allocate(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    );
}
```

The service should use the **existing** `SyirkahResultCalculator` for profit/loss allocation rather than creating another nisbah engine.

---

# 3. Profit allocation

For liquidation profit:

```text
Net realization
       -
Opening capital
       =
Liquidation profit
       ↓
Existing SyirkahResultCalculator
       ↓
Partner profit allocations
```

For example:

```text
Net realization       130
Opening capital       100
Profit                 30

Partner A 40%          12
Partner B 60%          18
```

The result is then converted into the already-established `PartnerDistributionObligation`.

```java
private List<PartnerDistributionObligation> createProfitDistributions(
        SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
        ProfitSharingResult allocation
) {
    return allocation.allocations().stream()
            .filter(a -> a.amount().signum() > 0)
            .map(a -> PartnerDistributionObligation.calculated(
                    result.liquidationId(),
                    result.contractId(),
                    result.contractVersion(),
                    a.partyId(),
                    a.amount()
            ))
            .toList();
}
```

The exact factory should follow the existing `PartnerDistributionObligation` API if it already has a different constructor/factory.

---

# 4. Capital return is separate

This is the more important part.

For:

```text
Opening capital = 100
Net realization = 130
Profit = 30
```

the obligations are:

```text
Profit distribution = 30
Capital return      = 100
```

**Not:**

```text
Partner payout = 130
```

Create a separate obligation:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.capital;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.time.Instant;
import java.util.Objects;

public final class PartnerCapitalReturnObligation {

    public enum Status {
        CALCULATED,
        APPROVED,
        POSTED,
        SETTLED,
        CANCELLED
    }

    private final String obligationId;
    private final String liquidationId;
    private final String partyId;
    private final BigDecimal capitalAmount;

    private Status status;
    private String approvedBy;
    private Instant approvedAt;
    private String postedJournalEntryId;
    private Instant postedAt;

    public PartnerCapitalReturnObligation(
            String obligationId,
            String liquidationId,
            String partyId,
            BigDecimal capitalAmount
    ) {
        require(obligationId, "Obligation ID");
        require(liquidationId, "Liquidation ID");
        require(partyId, "Party ID");

        if (capitalAmount == null || capitalAmount.signum() <= 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    "Capital return amount must be positive"
            );
        }

        this.obligationId = obligationId;
        this.liquidationId = liquidationId;
        this.partyId = partyId;
        this.capitalAmount = capitalAmount;
        this.status = Status.CALCULATED;
    }

    public void approve(String approver) {
        require(approver, "Approver");

        if (status != Status.CALCULATED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return can only be approved from CALCULATED"
            );
        }

        status = Status.APPROVED;
        approvedBy = approver;
        approvedAt = Instant.now();
    }

    public void markPosted(
            String journalEntryId,
            String postedBy
    ) {
        require(journalEntryId, "Journal entry ID");
        require(postedBy, "Posted by");

        if (status != Status.APPROVED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return can only be posted from APPROVED"
            );
        }

        status = Status.POSTED;
        postedJournalEntryId = journalEntryId;
        postedAt = Instant.now();
    }

    public void settle() {
        if (status != Status.POSTED) {
            throw new IllegalStateException(
                    "Capital return can only be settled from POSTED"
            );
        }

        status = Status.SETTLED;
    }

    public String getObligationId() {
        return obligationId;
    }

    public String getLiquidationId() {
        return liquidationId;
    }

    public String getPartyId() {
        return partyId;
    }

    public BigDecimal getCapitalAmount() {
        return capitalAmount;
    }

    public Status getStatus() {
        return status;
    }

    private static void require(String value, String name) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(value, name + " cannot be null");

        if (value.isBlank()) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    name + " cannot be blank"
            );
        }
    }
}
```

---

# 5. Capital return calculation

Capital return must use the **opening capital position**, not the profit allocation.

For each partner:

```text
returnable capital
    =
opening capital
    - capital impairments
    - previous capital returns
```

The liquidation service should therefore consume the frozen close position.

Conceptually:

```java
private BigDecimal calculateReturnableCapital(
        PartnerClosePositionSnapshot position
) {
    return position.openingCapital()
            .add(position.capitalContributions())
            .subtract(position.capitalReturns())
            .subtract(position.capitalImpairments());
}
```

For a full liquidation, that becomes the maximum capital-return obligation.

---

# 6. Loss is different

Suppose:

```text
Opening capital       100
Net realization        70
Loss                   30
```

We do **not** create:

```text
Capital return = 70
Loss distribution = 30
```

as two independent payouts without reconciliation.

Instead:

```text
Capital position
        ↓
Loss allocation policy
        ↓
Remaining capital
        ↓
Capital return
```

For a normal capital-based loss:

```text
Partner A capital     40
Partner B capital     60

Loss                  30

A absorbs              12
B absorbs              18

Remaining capital:
A                      28
B                      42
```

Therefore:

```text
Capital return:
A                       28
B                       42
```

This is exactly why **loss allocation and capital return cannot be one operation**.

---

# 7. Reconciliation

Now we need the invariant that prevents money from being created or lost during liquidation.

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public record SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
        BigDecimal netRealization,
        BigDecimal totalProfitDistribution,
        BigDecimal totalLossAbsorption,
        BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn,
        BigDecimal remainingBalance,
        boolean balanced,
        List<String> errors
) {

    public SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation {
        errors = List.copyOf(
                errors == null ? List.of() : errors
        );
    }

    public static SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation reconcile(
            BigDecimal netRealization,
            BigDecimal totalProfitDistribution,
            BigDecimal totalLossAbsorption,
            BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn
    ) {
        List<String> errors = new ArrayList<>();

        BigDecimal distributable =
                netRealization
                        .subtract(totalCapitalReturn);

        BigDecimal expectedDistribution =
                distributable.max(BigDecimal.ZERO);

        BigDecimal actualDistribution =
                totalProfitDistribution;

        if (expectedDistribution.compareTo(actualDistribution) != 0) {
            errors.add(
                    "Profit distribution does not reconcile with "
                            + "net realization after capital return"
            );
        }

        BigDecimal remainingBalance =
                netRealization
                        .subtract(totalCapitalReturn)
                        .subtract(totalProfitDistribution);

        boolean balanced =
                remainingBalance.signum() == 0
                        && errors.isEmpty();

        return new SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
                netRealization,
                totalProfitDistribution,
                totalLossAbsorption,
                totalCapitalReturn,
                remainingBalance,
                balanced,
                errors
        );
    }
}
```

However, for **loss**, we need a slightly different equation.

The stronger invariant is:

```text
net realization
=
capital returned
+
profit distributed
```

when the result is a profit.

For a loss:

```text
opening capital
-
loss absorption
=
capital returned
```

Therefore the final reconciliation should actually know the **opening capital** as well.

I'd refine the model to:

```java
public record SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
        BigDecimal openingCapital,
        BigDecimal netRealization,
        BigDecimal profitDistributed,
        BigDecimal lossAbsorbed,
        BigDecimal capitalReturned,
        BigDecimal remainingBalance,
        boolean balanced,
        List<String> errors
) {}
```

with invariants:

```text
PROFIT:

netRealization
=
openingCapital
+
profitDistributed
```

and:

```text
netRealization
=
capitalReturned
+
profitDistributed
```

while:

```text
LOSS:

openingCapital
=
netRealization
+
lossAbsorbed
```

and:

```text
netRealization
=
capitalReturned
```

assuming all remaining assets are returned.

---

# 8. Final liquidation equation

That gives us a very useful invariant:

```text
                 PROFIT
                   │
        ┌──────────┴──────────┐
        │                     │
Capital return          Profit distribution
        │                     │
        └──────────┬──────────┘
                   ↓
             Net realization
```

For loss:

```text
                 LOSS
                   │
        ┌──────────┴──────────┐
        │                     │
 Loss absorption        Capital return
        │                     │
        └──────────┬──────────┘
                   ↓
             Net realization
```

And **cash settlement is still downstream**:

```text
Liquidation result
       ↓
Obligations
       ↓
Approval
       ↓
Accounting posting
       ↓
Cash settlement
```

This preserves the distinction we already established between allocation and actual payment.

### The next implementation step

The next piece should now be **`SyirkahLiquidationAllocationServiceImpl` + the final reconciliation calculator**, which will combine:

- `SyirkahResultCalculator`
- `LossAllocationPolicyResolver`
- frozen `SyirkahCloseSnapshot`
- `PartnerDistributionObligation`
- `PartnerCapitalReturnObligation`
- conditional `SyirkahLossResponsibility`
- `SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation`

and make the whole liquidation calculation **idempotent and impossible to complete when the reconciliation does not balance**.

////////////////


## Next: `SyirkahLiquidationAllocationServiceImpl`

This is the orchestration boundary between the already-existing Syirkah calculation engine and liquidation obligations.

The important rule is:

> **Allocation may be recalculated safely, but a liquidation must never advance to settlement while its reconciliation is unbalanced.**

### 1. Repository for the allocation result

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.spi.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.SyirkahLiquidationAllocation;

import java.util.Optional;

public interface SyirkahLiquidationAllocationRepository {

    Uni<Optional<SyirkahLiquidationAllocation>> findByLiquidationId(
            String tenantId,
            String ledgerId,
            String liquidationId
    );

    Uni<Void> save(
            String tenantId,
            String ledgerId,
            SyirkahLiquidationAllocation allocation
    );
}
```

The database should enforce:

```sql
UNIQUE (
    tenant_id,
    ledger_id,
    liquidation_id
);
```

That gives us persistent idempotency rather than relying on an in-memory guard.

---

# 2. Reconciliation calculator

I would make this a pure domain service.

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.ArrayList;
import java.util.List;

public final class SyirkahLiquidationReconciliationCalculator {

    public SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation calculate(
            SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
            BigDecimal totalProfitDistribution,
            BigDecimal totalLossAbsorption,
            BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn
    ) {
        requireNonNegative(
                totalProfitDistribution,
                "Total profit distribution"
        );

        requireNonNegative(
                totalLossAbsorption,
                "Total loss absorption"
        );

        requireNonNegative(
                totalCapitalReturn,
                "Total capital return"
        );

        List<String> errors = new ArrayList<>();

        BigDecimal remainingBalance;

        if (result.isProfit()) {
            /*
             * Final assets must equal:
             *
             * original capital
             * + profit distributed
             *
             * and simultaneously:
             *
             * capital returned
             * + profit distributed
             */
            BigDecimal expectedProfit =
                    result.netRealization()
                            .subtract(result.originalCapital());

            if (expectedProfit.compareTo(totalProfitDistribution) != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Profit distribution does not equal liquidation profit"
                );
            }

            if (totalLossAbsorption.signum() != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Loss absorption must be zero for a profitable liquidation"
                );
            }

            BigDecimal expectedCapitalReturn =
                    result.originalCapital();

            if (expectedCapitalReturn.compareTo(totalCapitalReturn) != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Capital return does not equal returnable capital"
                );
            }

            remainingBalance =
                    result.netRealization()
                            .subtract(totalCapitalReturn)
                            .subtract(totalProfitDistribution);

        } else if (result.isLoss()) {
            /*
             * For loss:
             *
             * original capital
             * =
             * loss absorbed
             * + capital returned
             */
            BigDecimal expectedLoss =
                    result.originalCapital()
                            .subtract(result.netRealization());

            if (expectedLoss.compareTo(totalLossAbsorption) != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Loss absorption does not equal liquidation loss"
                );
            }

            if (totalProfitDistribution.signum() != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Profit distribution must be zero for a loss"
                );
            }

            BigDecimal expectedCapitalReturn =
                    result.netRealization();

            if (expectedCapitalReturn.compareTo(totalCapitalReturn) != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Capital return does not equal remaining net realization"
                );
            }

            remainingBalance =
                    result.netRealization()
                            .subtract(totalCapitalReturn);

        } else {
            /*
             * Break-even:
             *
             * original capital = capital returned
             */
            if (totalProfitDistribution.signum() != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Profit distribution must be zero at break-even"
                );
            }

            if (totalLossAbsorption.signum() != 0) {
                errors.add(
                        "Loss absorption must be zero at break-even"
                );
            }

            if (result.originalCapital()
                    .compareTo(totalCapitalReturn) != 0) {

                errors.add(
                        "Capital return does not equal original capital"
                );
            }

            remainingBalance =
                    result.netRealization()
                            .subtract(totalCapitalReturn);
        }

        boolean balanced =
                remainingBalance.signum() == 0
                        && errors.isEmpty();

        return new SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation(
                result.originalCapital(),
                result.netRealization(),
                totalProfitDistribution,
                totalLossAbsorption,
                totalCapitalReturn,
                remainingBalance,
                balanced,
                errors
        );
    }

    private static void requireNonNegative(
            BigDecimal value,
            String name
    ) {
        if (value == null || value.signum() < 0) {
            throw new IllegalArgumentException(
                    name + " must not be negative"
            );
        }
    }
}
```

### Important refinement

This calculator assumes the **whole net realization is ultimately allocated between capital return and result allocation**.

If the contract has retained business assets, restricted reserves, unresolved liabilities, or another disposition mechanism, that must be represented explicitly rather than allowing this calculator to silently balance by ignoring it.

---

# 3. Allocation service implementation

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.close.SyirkahCloseSnapshot;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.*;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.List;
import java.util.Objects;

public final class SyirkahLiquidationAllocationServiceImpl
        implements SyirkahLiquidationAllocationService {

    private final SyirkahLiquidationAllocationRepository allocationRepository;
    private final SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver resultPolicyResolver;
    private final SyirkahLiquidationReconciliationCalculator reconciliationCalculator;
    private final SyirkahPartnerAllocationService partnerAllocationService;
    private final SyirkahCapitalReturnCalculator capitalReturnCalculator;

    public SyirkahLiquidationAllocationServiceImpl(
            SyirkahLiquidationAllocationRepository allocationRepository,
            SyirkahLiquidationResultPolicyResolver resultPolicyResolver,
            SyirkahLiquidationReconciliationCalculator reconciliationCalculator,
            SyirkahPartnerAllocationService partnerAllocationService,
            SyirkahCapitalReturnCalculator capitalReturnCalculator
    ) {
        this.allocationRepository =
                Objects.requireNonNull(allocationRepository);

        this.resultPolicyResolver =
                Objects.requireNonNull(resultPolicyResolver);

        this.reconciliationCalculator =
                Objects.requireNonNull(reconciliationCalculator);

        this.partnerAllocationService =
                Objects.requireNonNull(partnerAllocationService);

        this.capitalReturnCalculator =
                Objects.requireNonNull(capitalReturnCalculator);
    }

    @Override
    public Uni<SyirkahLiquidationAllocation> allocate(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    ) {
        Objects.requireNonNull(liquidation);
        Objects.requireNonNull(result);
        Objects.requireNonNull(openingSnapshot);
        Objects.requireNonNull(contractVersion);

        return allocationRepository.findByLiquidationId(
                        liquidation.getTenantId(),
                        liquidation.getLedgerId(),
                        liquidation.getLiquidationId()
                )
                .chain(existing -> {
                    if (existing.isPresent()) {
                        return Uni.createFrom().item(existing.get());
                    }

                    return calculateAndPersist(
                            liquidation,
                            result,
                            openingSnapshot,
                            contractVersion
                    );
                });
    }

    private Uni<SyirkahLiquidationAllocation> calculateAndPersist(
            SyirkahLiquidation liquidation,
            SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
            SyirkahCloseSnapshot openingSnapshot,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    ) {
        return partnerAllocationService
                .allocate(
                        result,
                        contractVersion
                )
                .chain(partnerAllocation ->
                        capitalReturnCalculator.calculate(
                                result,
                                openingSnapshot,
                                partnerAllocation
                        )
                        .map(capitalReturns -> {

                            BigDecimal totalProfit =
                                    partnerAllocation.totalProfit();

                            BigDecimal totalLoss =
                                    partnerAllocation.totalLoss();

                            BigDecimal totalCapitalReturn =
                                    capitalReturns.totalAmount();

                            SyirkahLiquidationReconciliation reconciliation =
                                    reconciliationCalculator.calculate(
                                            result,
                                            totalProfit,
                                            totalLoss,
                                            totalCapitalReturn
                                    );

                            if (!reconciliation.balanced()) {
                                throw new IllegalStateException(
                                        "Liquidation reconciliation failed: "
                                                + String.join(
                                                "; ",
                                                reconciliation.errors()
                                        )
                                );
                            }

                            SyirkahLiquidationAllocation allocation =
                                    new SyirkahLiquidationAllocation(
                                            liquidation.getLiquidationId(),
                                            result,
                                            partnerAllocation
                                                    .profitDistributions(),
                                            capitalReturns.obligations(),
                                            partnerAllocation
                                                    .lossResponsibilities()
                                    );

                            return allocation;
                        })
                )
                .chain(allocation ->
                        allocationRepository.save(
                                liquidation.getTenantId(),
                                liquidation.getLedgerId(),
                                allocation
                        )
                        .replaceWith(allocation)
                );
    }
}
```

There is one deliberate architectural choice here:

**the allocation service does not post accounting journals.**

It creates a business result that can subsequently go through:

```text
allocation
   ↓
approval
   ↓
accounting policy
   ↓
journal
   ↓
settlement
```

---

# 4. Partner allocation port

Rather than embedding another profit-sharing implementation here:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import io.smallrye.mutiny.Uni;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.SyirkahContract;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.liquidation.SyirkahLiquidationResult;

public interface SyirkahPartnerAllocationService {

    Uni<PartnerAllocationResult> allocate(
            SyirkahLiquidationResult result,
            SyirkahContract.Version contractVersion
    );
}
```

Result:

```java
package tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.application.syirkah.liquidation;

import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.distribution.PartnerDistributionObligation;
import tech.kayys.syirkah.accounting.domain.syirkah.loss.SyirkahLossResponsibility;

import java.math.BigDecimal;
import java.util.List;

public record PartnerAllocationResult(
        List<PartnerDistributionObligation> profitDistributions,
        List<SyirkahLossResponsibility> lossResponsibilities,
        BigDecimal totalProfit,
        BigDecimal totalLoss
) {

    public PartnerAllocationResult {
        profitDistributions =
                List.copyOf(
                        profitDistributions == null
                                ? List.of()
                                : profitDistributions
                );

        lossResponsibilities =
                List.copyOf(
                        lossResponsibilities == null
                                ? List.of()
                                : lossResponsibilities
                );

        totalProfit =
                totalProfit == null
                        ? BigDecimal.ZERO
                        : totalProfit;

        totalLoss =
                totalLoss == null
                        ? BigDecimal.ZERO
                        : totalLoss;
    }
}
```

This lets the implementation delegate to the existing:

```text
SyirkahResultCalculator
        +
LossAllocationPolicyResolver
```

rather than creating a second calculation engine.
